v.story-open.intro.1.text: Open Sky Isles float above the clouds, and many of their words end in a long, open vowel.

v.story-open.intro.2.text: Here a vowel is free to say its own name, with no consonant door to shut it in.

v.story-open.intro.3.text: The next torn pages drifted up here, so climb the rope bridges and follow them.

v.story-open.open-one.1.text: The first island has a single vowel at the end of a word, and that vowel says its name.

v.story-open.open-one.2.text: Words like she and go open wide, so the vowel is the first sound you hear.

v.story-open.open-vcv.1.text: A robot clanks into a local hotel, and its name splits right after the open first vowel.

v.story-open.open-vcv.2.text: When a vowel stands alone at the end of the first part, it often says its own name, so read it long.

v.story-open.open-y.1.text: A baby bunny hops by a cloud, and its name ends with a y that sings a long e.

v.story-open.open-y.2.text: At the end of a word, y can take the long e sound, so listen for the bunny's name.

v.story-open.open-flex.1.text: A cabin floats in the clouds, but the first split does not match the sound.

v.story-open.open-flex.2.text: Flip the split to the other side, try again, and the word will click into place.

v.story-open.finale.1.text: The Open Sky Isles are bright again, and the pages ride the wind like kites.

v.story-open.finale.2.text: The Keeper says, 'The next forest hides silent e's, and they change the vowels around them.'
